Setup (the role list itself is secret). This game has 13 players. Its roles were drawn at random by the standard setup: 3 or 4 Yakuza for 13 players (each about half the time); 0 to 4 Neutrals, usually 2, at most 2 of them Neutral killers; the rest are Good: at least 5 Village roles that aren't Outsiders (at least 2 of them Investigative, 1 Killing and 1 Protective), plus any mix of Village roles and up to 2 Outsiders. Roles may repeat, except unique ones (R2). The roles are picked so that the sides are roughly balanced by strength: e.g. more Yakuza tend to get weaker roles. This setup never uses these roles, so nobody has them: Vanilla Villager, Grunt. Results that name a role (including fakes) never name them either. Separately, traits (R24) are dealt: each player, independently of everyone else, has 0, 1 or 2 traits, a 1/3 chance each (rarely fewer, when no other trait fits them). Which traits are dealt is drawn to help balance the sides; some traits can go only to Village players.

DeathOlivia died (killed by Werewolf). Their role isn't revealed. Their last will: "Olivia: Seer (Good). Random pairs: N1 Niaj/Bob DIFFERENT. N2 Niaj/Judy SAME (Judy was the Saint, so Niaj read Good). N3: role-blocked (token unspent). N4: Carol/Niaj DIFFERENT. Niaj was Good, so Carol is NOT Good. Only Carol and I are left and the game didn't end, so Carol is the Yakuza or the Werewolf. N4 killed Grace with the Werewolf and Niaj with the Katana. Carol's Auditor claim was cover. Nobody died on N5, an odd night when a Werewolf can't act, which fits Carol being the Werewolf. D3: Innocent on Mallory, Guilty on Bob. D4: Guilty on Mallory. D5 and D6: nominated Carol each time; every nomination failed with 1 Yes."
The game is over. Winners: Carol.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewCarol, the Werewolf, won alone. Her one big play decided the game. On Night 2 she rampaged at Judy's house, guessing that Judy, who had led Day 2, would draw visitors. She was right: Judy (Saint), Alice and Heidi all died, and Frank (Yakuza) died of heartbreak because he was bonded to Alice. After that she claimed Auditor, a role nobody could check. She voted with the majority and stayed out of the Jester-revenge draw, and nobody ever made her prove the claim. The Yakuza had four passive roles (Wiretap and three Informants) and only the Katana to kill with. They coordinated cleanly in night chat but bled players. Dave's census counts true alignment, so it beat Bob's fake Notorious trait. Then on his own trial day Bob privately offered Mallory a vote trade, Mallory exposed it, and he was hanged. On Night 3 Niaj spent a token to visit both Erin and Grace with his Enforcer and killed Erin, who held the Katana. Mallory, a Hitman, faked a Jester claim to survive Day 3 and helped kill Dave on Night 3. On Day 4, with 5 alive, the Village hanged her. A Hitman never blocks wins, so the Village lost the Day's hang and still faced Grace (the last Yakuza, who had claimed nothing until pressed) and Carol, whose claimed Auditor result from Night 3 never appeared. On Night 4 Niaj sent a Strong Enforcer attack at Grace and Carol that would have killed Carol, but his hidden Drowsy trait blocked it. Grace's Katana killed Niaj and Carol's rampage killed Grace. Olivia never spent her Seer token, and with only two players left she could never get the 2 Yes votes to put Carol on trial.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: low, rules ambiguityNight 5: only Carol was alive besides Olivia, so the Seer's random pair of two other players couldn't be drawn. The Seer text doesn't cover this case; the Census Taker's text does ('the group is smaller'). The moderator flagged it and gave no result, which was sensible, but the rule should say what happens.
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Informant text says it sees 'how every player voted' and doesn't say whether that is the vote cast or the vote as counted. The Fixer and Merciful texts are what imply it reports the counted vote. In Bob's trial Mallory (Merciful) said 'Guilty' in public, but the Informant report showed Innocent. Erin and Grace concluded she had lied about her vote and planned Day 4 around that. The ruling was correct, but the Informant's own text should say it reports votes as counted.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 3 Carol said the only Village roles with no night action are Saint, Mayor and Sniper. She left out Magistrate and the passive-result roles (Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Scout, Bloodhound need no action), so her case against Mallory's 'no night action' claim was stronger than the rules support.
Game over
